solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Familiar with second-hand book? Not me

indicators.note: 'Not me' tells the solver to drop the letters spelling the pronoun from the word just before it

blocks.note: second-hand goods are used ones
a tome is a large book
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Someone recognises a second-hand book but insists it was never theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: TOME loses ME to leave TO, giving USED TO.
explanation.definitionFit: To be used to something is to be accustomed to it, an idiom for being familiar with it.

clue.text: Catching train, visit required

indicators.note: catching means seizing and holding inside

blocks.note: a stay is a visit
to train is to tutor

explanation.surface: Catching a train is needed for the visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' is a verb, to teach, not the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutory means laid down by law, so mandatory or required.

clue.text: Sort of turn into the same couple

indicators.note: into means placed inside the following word

blocks.note: DO, short for ditto, means the same
a U-turn is a sort of turn

explanation.surface: A double act performs the same routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a pair, especially of performers, which is a couple.

clue.text: City banks after gold

indicators.note: after says the piece for tilting is placed second, behind the metal

blocks.note: OR is gold in heraldry
an aircraft banks or leans when turning

explanation.surface: A city's banks are chasing gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' is a verb, tilting, not financial institutions.
explanation.definitionFit: Orléans is a city in France on the Loire, so a city by example.

clue.text: Spanish boy needs a lot of alcohol? LOL, no!

indicators.note: 'no' after the internet abbreviation says those letters are refused, taken out of the word before

blocks.note: a lot means much
taken as written
taken as written, the letters to strike out

explanation.surface: A Spanish lad needs plenty to drink, and someone texting 'LOL' disapproves.
explanation.walkthrough: LOL is internet slang for 'laughing out loud', but here its three letters are simply removed one by one from the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Muchacho is the Spanish word for a boy or lad, borrowed into English.

clue.text: Music of Island Records?

blocks.note: surface reading: the record label, issuing music
setter's reading: a traffic island and where it sits

explanation.walkthrough: A traffic island sits in the centre of a street, and the phrase also names bland mainstream pop, MOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-of-the-road is the genre label for inoffensive mainstream easy-listening music.

clue.text: Lead found in artificial apple

indicators.note: found in means located inside

blocks.note: cod as an adjective means fake or mock
the lead in a film is its star

explanation.surface: Lead discovered in a fake apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests the metal; it is the leading actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Costard is an old English variety of large cooking apple.

clue.text: Sailor's single subject a constant source of conflict

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
single means one
a subject is a topic
K is a symbol for a constant in science

explanation.surface: A sailor's one topic of conversation keeps causing rows.
explanation.definitionFit: A bone to pick is a grievance one wants to raise, an idiom for a point of dispute.

clue.text: Jack is into baking

indicators.note: into means placed inside the following word

blocks.note: baking as in very warm
taken as written

explanation.surface: Jack has a passion for baking.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack looks like a name; it is the verb to jack up, lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack a car is to raise it, so to hoist it.

clue.text: Was a singer about to get rumbled?

blocks.note: CA, short for circa, means about
thunder rumbles or rolls

explanation.surface: A singer is about to be found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rumbled' reads as British slang for exposed or caught out; here it is the noise of thunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To carol is to sing joyfully, so someone who carolled was acting as a singer.

clue.text: Wooden tee's hard to accept

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: hard means solid
tee is the spelt-out name of the letter T

explanation.surface: A wooden golf tee proves hard to accept.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as 'tee is [for] hard to accept': SOLID takes in T. The grammar is a little loose, since the tee seems to do the accepting.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden manner is stiff and unemotional, which is what stolid describes.

clue.text: Old house — or seats in it?

blocks.note: surface reading: an aged building or former legislature
setter's reading: seats as bottoms, sitting in the chamber

explanation.walkthrough: The Rump Parliament was what remained of the English House of Commons after Pride's Purge in 1648; a rump is also a backside, a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: It was a historical House of Commons, so an old house in the parliamentary sense.

clue.text: A risk to poor in each reform

indicators.note: poor here means in bad shape, so these letters are reworked
in means placed inside the following word

blocks.note: a as in 'five pounds a day' means per
EA is the abbreviation for each
the letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: A reform that endangers the poor in every case.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening A is not taken literally; it is the 'a' of rates, meaning per. The mixed RISK TO then sits inside EA.
explanation.definitionFit: Perestroika was Gorbachev's programme of restructuring the Soviet economy, a historic reform.

clue.text: Swap letters in answer

blocks.note: first meaning: exchange letters with a pen friend
second meaning: match or agree with, as a description answers to someone

explanation.surface: An instruction to switch letters around inside a solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swap letters' looks like a wordplay instruction for an anagram but is a plain definition of writing to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondents exchange letters, and to correspond also means to match, as one thing answers to another.

clue.text: Leave nothing to talk about

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for chatter is read backwards

blocks.note: nothing is zero, shaped like O
to yak is to chatter

explanation.surface: Something not worth discussing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: ORAL is a tempting wrong answer from 'talk'.
explanation.definitionFit: An okay is permission, as is leave in the sense of being allowed to do something.

clue.text: They do supply cash one always splits

indicators.note: supply read as in a supple way, so the letters bend into a new order
to split something is to come between its parts

blocks.note: the letters to be mixed
one is the Roman numeral I
always means ever

explanation.surface: Some people provide the money that one person always divides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is not provide but the adverb from supple, read sup-ply.
explanation.definitionFit: Achievers are people who get things done, doers, which is what 'they do' describes.

clue.text: Witnesses close to police, of course

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: the end of police
of course is an emphatic yes

explanation.surface: Witnesses stay near the police, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness something is to see it, so witnesses as a verb means eyes, watches.

clue.text: Ace up one's sleeve

blocks.note: first meaning: excellent, in slang
second meaning: hidden from view

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the card sharp's ace up the sleeve; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of sight is dated slang for fantastic, and something concealed in a sleeve cannot be seen.

clue.text: Lavish spread put on, sandwiches extremely large

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so the letters are rearranged
sandwiches means holding something in the middle
extremely points to the extremes, the outer letters, of the next word

blocks.note: the letters to be mixed
the first and last letters of large

explanation.surface: A lavish buffet put on, with sandwiches that are very large.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means rich and luxurious, a synonym of lavish.

clue.text: Plump to accept stories; hope it works

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in

blocks.note: plump means fat
lore is a body of traditional stories

explanation.surface: Someone opts to accept the stories, hoping it pays off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump' looks like the verb to choose; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Floreat is Latin for 'may it flourish', a wish for success, as in school mottoes.

clue.text: Little sweets with lots in them

definitions.text: Little sweets with lots in them

blocks.note: surface reading: large quantities, as of filling
setter's reading: a person's lot or destiny, the prediction on the paper slip inside

explanation.walkthrough: A lot is one's fate, and these crisp sweet biscuits each hide a slip of paper predicting it.
explanation.definitionFit: These small sweet biscuits served in Chinese restaurants each contain a printed prediction of the eater's future.

clue.text: Trust footballers? It's hard

blocks.note: the FA, Football Association, governs English football
taken as written
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Trusting footballers is difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith is confidence or belief in someone, a synonym of trust.

clue.text: Male put out after sex

indicators.note: after says the piece for annoying is placed second, behind the Latin word

blocks.note: sex is Latin for six, Roman numeral VI
to put out is to annoy

explanation.surface: A man left annoyed after an encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: Sex is not the act here but the Latin number six.
explanation.definitionFit: Virile describes masculine vigour, so it serves as an adjective for male.

clue.text: Flower pots are inclined to produce poisonous plant

indicators.note: to pot something is to put it inside a pot, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Oder runs between Germany and Poland
to be inclined is to lean

explanation.surface: Pots of flowers lean over and yield a toxic plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' wants to be the plant; it is a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is an ornamental shrub every part of which is toxic, an example of a poisonous plant.

clue.text: New writer's game

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
the writer refers to themselves: I'm, writer is

explanation.surface: A new author's game.
explanation.definitionFit: Nim is a game of strategy in which players take turns removing objects from heaps.

clue.text: Run into drunk that we'd beaten

indicators.note: into means placed inside the following letters
drunk letters stagger about out of order

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: A drunk collides with someone the speaker thought defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be thwarted is to be foiled or defeated, so it is a synonym of beaten.

clue.text: Most docile volunteers found carrying spades

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within

blocks.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
found as in came across, met
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: The gentlest volunteers turn up carrying shovels.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of tame means the most gentle or docile.
